deviations.what: enrol-models responses list actor ids and actions (create/update), not revisions
deviations.reason: actors carry no revision field in the store; only workflows do (repoint-actor returns the new workflow revision). Adding actor revisions is a store/model change beyond this spec. Operator approved.

deviations.what: model_gateways is a list of 'machine=URL' strings, not a machine->URL object
deviations.reason: variables hold only a JSON scalar or a list of scalars (culture_rules/model/variable.py validate_variable_value); objects are refused. Operator chose the list form (d3 a) over extending variables.

deviations.what: the actor guards also cover restore and import (model_taken) and delete (actor_in_use, --force); repoint checks the target can run the repointed actions (llm.complete needs an endpoint actor; other kinds must match the action's actor kind); the run-time model_taken check refuses only actors newer than the holder (created_at, then id), so the oldest keeps serving
deviations.reason: code review of PR #72: restore/import could create a second holder, delete removed an in-use actor that disable refused, repoint accepted a target that fails at run time, and the symmetric run-time check stopped every actor on a shared model; approved by the operator 2026-10-20

deviations.what: the run-time model_taken winner is the holder with the lowest actor id, not the oldest by created_at (d5): actor documents carry no creation time
deviations.reason: d5 named created_at, but actor documents store no created_at (only updated_at, which changes on every save); the lowest id is deterministic, so every node picks the same winner
